note: Evidence: MusicBrainz work and release data through the shared fetcher, Wikipedia work lists and discographies, a few label and review pages, web searches. Apple lookups were blocked or queued for most of the run and were dropped; nothing here rests on Apple data. Gap additions (imslpPage null): Dubois Cantilène; Juon String Quartet Op. 11 (unpublished) and Legende Op. 83; Kahn Piano Trio No. 4 Op. 72; Reinecke Quartets Op. 16 and Op. 287; Rimsky-Korsakov Four Variations on a Chorale; Rubinstein Piano Quartet Op. 55bis (string version published with the wind quintet in 1860; the composer's own authorship is not confirmed, confidence low). Judgement calls: Kahn's Serenade Op. 73 is printed for oboe, horn and piano with violin, viola or cello as alternatives and is recorded as a horn trio, so it is listed as violin, horn, piano (medium). Dubois's Piano Quintet is printed for oboe (or second violin or clarinet). Juon's Op. 39 is B minor on IMSLP and the Challenge disc (Wikipedia says D major). Juon's Trio-Miniaturen are entered in the clarinet version that Trio Catch recorded. Skipped as unrecorded in the original scoring: Dubois Hymne nuptial, Méditation-prière and Deux pièces canoniques (only transcriptions or a reduced version recorded). 'None found' is weaker for Glière (quartets 3-4, sextets), Rimsky-Korsakov (sextet, quartet in G) and Rubinstein (piano trios, quintets, sextet, quartets Op. 47 No. 2, Op. 90, Op. 106): the MusicBrainz release scans were partial (Rimsky-Korsakov 226 of 592, Glière 53 of 57). Rachmaninoff's two quartets are unfinished two-movement works recorded as they stand. Wind-only works (Reinecke Op. 188, 216, 271, 274; Herzogenberg Op. 43, 61; Juon Op. 51, 73, 84; Rimsky-Korsakov and Rubinstein piano-and-wind quintets; Dubois Dixtuor, ten players) are out of scope. Glière's 12 Duos Op. 49 (violin catalogue 463) are a duo.
